note: XXVII: the Count on the bridge — rising, struck, dust — silhouettes against the sun (Ian, 21 Nov) · retake: kneeling; knives highly reflective (Ian)
style: An oil painting in colour of 1893 matching the first reference image: the same great ancient stone bridge with carved gargoyles over a deep snowy gorge, the same ruined castle on its crag, the same blood-red sunset sky with the sun low and large, in the manner of Thomas Cole. The figures are dark silhouettes against the setting sun, with detail only in the rim light. Strong value contrast, loose visible brushwork. No blood, no gore. No text, signature or border.

beats.text: Shot: wide, on the bridge deck. A long open rectangular wooden box lies overturned on the snowy paving, earth spilled out of it, and a tall gaunt figure in a long dark coat is still on his knees half out of it, struggling to rise, one hand braced on the stones, not yet standing, a black silhouette against the huge setting sun. Around him on the bridge: men with levelled rifles, mounted gypsies in sheepskins reining back, a halted cart, all in silhouette with rim light, the carved balustrade and gargoyles catching the red light.

Shot: wide, on the bridge deck, silhouettes against the huge setting sun. Two men strike at the tall kneeling figure beside the overturned box: one sweeps a great curved Gurkha blade, the other drives down a long bowie knife; both blades are polished mirror-bright steel, highly reflective, blazing white where they catch the setting sun, with bright glints and streaks of reflected light; the kneeling figure arched back, all three black against the red disc of the sun, the other men and the gypsies frozen around them, the castle on its crag beyond.
